subject: Mutual Action Plan: evaluation milestones, commits & true-up language
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP + eval plan + proposed commercial milestones

Sam — great talking earlier. Per our conversation, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (Orbit_MAP_v3.xlsx) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial checkpoints: a 30-day POC, 60-day extended eval, then a ramp/commit decision at day 90. Key commercial hooks in the draft: a demo milestone (30d) activates evaluation credits; at 60d we expect 50% of target throughput; at 90d a commit review where discounts kick in based on commit size and ramp velocity.

High-level commercial proposal:
- 12-month committed spend tiers with stepped discounts at $100k, $250k, $500k
- Early ramp discount (first 3 months) to absorb integration costs
- Quarterly true-ups for overage/under-usage; price protection for 12 months from signing

We want to avoid ambiguous "usage" definitions in the contract; see the MAP sheet for suggested token definitions (inference tokens only, exclude logs/backups). Can your procurement/legal folks review the MAP and the SOW draft and flag any must-haves?

If this looks good, can we lock the MAP timelines into the SOW so procurement can map approval dates?

Thanks — Rishi

Attachments: Orbit_MAP_v3.xlsx, SOW_draft_v1.docx

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Krista Lee <krista.lee@orbit-analytics.com>, procurement@orbit-analytics.com
Date: 2026-04-19T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan + proposed commercial milestones

Rishi — thanks for the draft. We like the MAP structure and the staged milestones, but legal has pushed back on a few commercial points (attached PDF with redlines):

1) True-up cadence: Our procurement requests monthly true-ups rather than quarterly. They want closer visibility for budget forecasting.
2) Price protection: We want a 24-month price protection on committed rates (not 12).
3) Usage definition: We're asking to include inference + embeddings + internal batch jobs under the definition of usage. Excluding logs/backups is fine.
4) Remedies: We asked for a cap on retroactive true-ups to avoid surprise billing months later.

We can be flexible on discounts, but any change to cadence or price-protection period needs to be reflected in the SOW and the order form.

Attached: Orbit_legal_redlines.pdf

Can we set a short meeting between legal teams? Krista is cc'd.

— Sam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orbit redlines — negotiation posture and proposed language

Team — forwarding Orbit's redlines. Key asks from the customer that impact economics: monthly true-ups (they want), 24-month price protection (pushy), and a broad usage definition (includes embeddings & batch jobs).

My suggested positions:
- True-ups: accept quarterly true-ups but offer a monthly reporting cadence with billing only quarterly (compromise gives procurement visibility without monthly invoices).
- Price protection: counter with 15 months price protection tied to committed spend bands; if they sign at $500k+ we can extend to 24 months.
- Usage definition: accept inference + embeddings, but explicitly exclude internal backfills and offline training. Add a definition for "billable tokens" with examples.
- Retroactive caps: propose a 30-day lookback for adjustments; any adjustments older than 30 days require mutual written confirmation.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft precise "billable tokens" wording we can insert into SOW (I'll copy standard language).
- Monica: prepare ramp verification steps for the MAP (how we validate throughput milestones).
- Rishi: can you run price-protection ladder scenarios with finance (examples for 12/15/24 months at each tier)?

I plan to send a compromise note to Sam/Krista this afternoon. Thoughts?

— Neha

(On internal thread) Attachment: none

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbit-analytics.com>, Krista Lee <krista.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, procurement@orbit-analytics.com
Date: 2026-04-20T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan + proposed commercial milestones — compromise proposal

Sam/Krista — thanks for the quick review and the redlines. We appreciate Orbit's priorities and have a compromise proposal that keeps the MAP timeline intact while addressing procurement and legal concerns: 

1) True-ups: monthly reporting + quarterly billing/true-ups. We will provide detailed monthly usage reports within 7 business days after month-end. Billing adjustments (credits/invoices) will be applied quarterly.

2) Price protection: standard 15 months price protection on committed unit pricing. If Orbit executes >= $500k committed ARR at signing, Redwood will extend price protection to 24 months.

3) Usage definition: billable usage = inference tokens + embeddings + API batch requests used for production inference. Excluded: internal offline model training, retention/backup logs, and tooling overhead. We will add explicit examples in the SOW for clarity.

4) Retroactive adjustments cap: adjustments may be applied up to 30 days after the month in which usage occurred; exceptions require mutual written agreement.

5) MAP tie-ins: milestone acceptance (30/60/90 days) will trigger evaluation credits or invoice milestones as listed in the MAP. We propose the SOW reference the MAP spreadsheet by filename and HubSpot deal id to ensure alignment.

If Orbit is okay with this approach we will: (a) drop updated language into the SOW (SOW_draft_v1.docx), (b) prepare the order form with the commit tiers and conditional 24-month protection clause, and (c) share a DocuSign for signature.

Please confirm by EOD Wednesday 4/22 so we can keep the MAP timeline (POC next Monday).

Thanks — Neha

Attachments: SOW_draft_v1.docx

From: Krista Lee <krista.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: procurement@orbit-analytics.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan + proposed commercial milestones — compromise proposal

Neha — appreciate the clear compromise. Orbit legal/procurement are supportive of the middle ground with two small asks before we sign: 

• Add a sentence clarifying that "internal offline model training" refers to training runs not initiated by or billed through the Redwood API and that retroactively-detected training runs will not be billed.
• For the 30-day adjustments cap, include a mutual audit clause allowing Orbit to request a one-time reconciliation for prior months within 60 days if there is reason to suspect material under-reporting.

If you can accept those two tweaks, we can route the SOW and order form to signature. Krista — will you send the final DocuSign link when ready.

— Krista

(On quoted text)
> On Mon, Apr 20, 2026 at 2:03 PM PDT, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Sam/Krista — thanks for the quick review and the redlines. ...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit agreement — final steps and internal checklist

Team — Orbit accepted the compromise with the two small tweaks (Krista's asks). Next steps:

1) Marissa: add explicit "billable token" examples and the "internal offline training" clarifier into SOW_draft_v1.docx and mark changes in redline.
2) Monica: update MAP verification bucket to include API telemetry checkpoints (timestamped throughput snapshots) and an acceptance sign-off template.
3) Rishi: finalize commit-tier pricing tables for 12/15/24 months scenarios and upload to the deal in HubSpot (deal id 67890). Finance will review before we publish the order form.
4) I'll prep the final SOW + order form and circulate DocuSign (expected EOD 4/23). DocuSign link will be posted in the thread and HubSpot.

I noted procurement asked for monthly visibility — we already committed to monthly reporting with quarterly billing, so be prepared to supply the month-end CSV export.

Thanks everyone — looks like we remain on-track for the POC next week.

— Neha
